description: Port from Electron to Tauri, done in place so the app stays launchable at every commit. Phase 1 builds src/renderer/ with Vite and Phase 2 collapses host access into one platform shim (source PRD: tasks/prd-renderer-decoupling.md). Phase 3 runs the torrent engine as a Node sidecar, Phase 4 ports src/main/ to Rust under Tauri, and Phase 5 covers casting, external players, codecs, and signing (source: docs/init.md, docs/README.md).

conventions.typecheck: This repo has no TypeScript. 'Typecheck passes' means `npm test`, which runs `standard` and `depcheck`.
conventions.smokeTest: 'Smoke test passes' means the six-step manual smoke test defined under 'Standard smoke test' in tasks/prd-renderer-decoupling.md. This is an Electron desktop app, so UI verification is that manual smoke test run via `npm start` -- NOT browser automation and NOT the dev-browser skill.
conventions.babelConfig: The Babel JSX config lives in the `babel` key of package.json, not in a `.babelrc` file. It is `@babel/plugin-transform-react-jsx` with `useBuiltIns: true`.
conventions.esmOrder: ESM conversion runs TOP-DOWN (entry point first, lib/ last). Babel compiles `export default X` to `exports.default = X`, so a still-CommonJS consumer that does `require('./x')` breaks. The reverse (ESM importing CommonJS) is safe via Babel's `_interopRequireDefault`. Converting consumers before their dependencies is therefore the only order that keeps the app launchable at every commit per FR-2.
conventions.invariant: FR-2: the Electron app must launch and pass the smoke test at every commit. A commit that leaves the app broken is not a valid commit.
conventions.cssFrozen: FR-14: no CSS file may be modified. No change to visual design or user-facing behaviour beyond the telemetry removal in US-002. This is otherwise a pure refactor.
conventions.webtorrentJsExempt: FR-4: src/renderer/webtorrent.js is never converted to ESM, never passed through Vite, and never migrated to the shim. It keeps building through Babel and loading via static/webtorrent.html unchanged.
conventions.deferredCasualties: After US-002 deletes telemetry, exactly two deferred-casualty files remain exempt from the shim and the lint rule: `src/renderer/webtorrent.js` and `src/renderer/lib/cast.js`. `controllers/audio-tracks-controller.js` is also a deferred casualty but imports nothing restricted, so it needs no exemption.
conventions.phases: US-001..US-017 are Phase 1 (Vite), US-018..US-035 Phase 2 (platform shim), US-036..US-049 Phase 3 (Node sidecar), US-050..US-073 Phase 4 (Rust host under Tauri), US-074..US-086 Phase 5 (casting, external players, codecs, signing). The phase table in docs/README.md is the summary; docs/init.md is the original plan.
conventions.engineTransport: Phase 3 decision: the renderer connects to the Node sidecar directly over a localhost WebSocket. ipc-engine.js becomes a WebSocket client and stops using ipcRenderer; the host only spawns the sidecar and reports its port and token via ipc-os.getEngineEndpoint(). The wt-* channel names and payloads are unchanged -- see the protocol tables in docs/platform-shim.md.
conventions.dualHost: Phase 4 decision: src-tauri/ grows alongside src/main/, both loading the same Vite bundle, with the shim implementation selected at build time. Electron stays launchable until the single cutover story (US-072). This is what keeps FR-2 true through the host swap.
conventions.rustChecks: For stories that touch src-tauri/, the Rust equivalent of typecheck is `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test`, run from src-tauri/. The JS checks (`npm test`) still apply on top.
conventions.manualStories: A story marked `"manual": true` needs an attended session -- a real app window, a packaged build, a signing certificate, or hardware on the local network -- and is excluded from the headless ralph loop.

Records the mechanism that selects a shim implementation at build time -- a Vite alias or conditional entry -- and why it is build-time rather than runtime
Records the Tauri major version targeted and the minimum toolchain versions

userStories.notes: Docs only, as AC-7 requires. ADR-014 records: (1) dual host -- src-tauri/ and src/main/ both launchable through Phase 4, same Vite output and same static/main.html, with US-072 the single cutover that flips the default and deletes src/main/; (2) build-time shim selection via a Vite resolveId plugin keyed on WT_HOST (default electron), rewriting lib/platform/<mod>.js to lib/platform/tauri/<mod>.js -- a resolve.alias entry cannot do it, because alias find patterns match the specifier as written and the barrel imports its siblings relatively; build-time because a runtime branch cannot produce a loadable Tauri bundle at all (require('electron') would survive into it), keeps ADR-009's boundary enforceable, does not triple what each story must keep working, and lets nodeIntegration die by construction; (3) Tauri 2 with the v2 plugin set, Rust >= 1.77.2 (developed on 1.97.1), Node >= 20.19 for Vite 8, Xcode CLT/WKWebView on macOS, MSVC + WebView2 on Windows, webkit2gtk-4.1 + libsoup3 on Linux; (4) casualties -- enableBlinkFeatures: 'AudioVideoTracks' has no WKWebView or WebKitGTK equivalent, so multi-audio switching goes (US-082) and, more seriously, the unguarded videoTracks/audioTracks reads at player-page.js:185-191 would throw in onLoadedMetadata and break playback startup (US-081); nodeIntegration and contextIsolation are lost by construction. Listed in docs/adr/INDEX.md. npm test 1736/1736 with lint and depcheck clean.
